pages.title: Preventing damage to the hood and support struts
pages.text:
4-2. Simple inspection and parts replacement

NOTICE
Preventing damage to the hood and damper struts

• When closing the hood, do not press down hard, for example by putting your body weight on it. This may dent the hood.
• The hood has damper struts to support it. Observe the following to prevent damage or malfunction:
  – Do not allow foreign material such as pieces of plastic, stickers or adhesive to stick to the rod portion of a strut.
  – Do not touch the rod with work gloves or similar items.
  – Do not attach accessories other than genuine Lexus accessories to the hood.
  – Do not place your hand on a strut or apply force to it sideways.

Printed page 234.

FLOOR JACK

When lifting the vehicle with a floor jack, position the jack at the correct location. Incorrect positioning may damage the vehicle or cause injury.

pages.title: Warnings when lifting the vehicle
pages.text:
4-2. Simple inspection and parts replacement

WARNING
When lifting the vehicle

Observe the following precautions to reduce the risk of death or serious injury:

• Lift the vehicle using a floor jack of the type shown in the illustration.
• Before using a floor jack, carefully read the instruction manual supplied with it.
• Do not use the jack supplied with the vehicle for this operation. The vehicle may fall.
• Never place any part of your body underneath, or crawl under, a vehicle supported only by a floor jack.
• Use the floor jack and vehicle jack stands on a firm, level floor without an incline.
• Do not start the engine while the vehicle is raised.
• Park the vehicle on firm, level ground, firmly apply the parking brake and move the shift lever to P.
• Always position the floor jack correctly at the jacking point. Lifting with the jack incorrectly positioned can damage the vehicle, and the vehicle may fall off the jack.
• Do not raise the vehicle with occupants inside.
• Do not place objects above or beneath the floor jack when lifting the vehicle.

Printed page 236.
